full_judgment:
Md. Ali Asgar Khan, J:- This rule on an application filed under section 561A of the Code of Criminal Procedure was issued calling upon the opposite parties to show cause as to why the proceeding in C.R. case No Class, Area 3 Mymensingh should not be quashed. 

 2. Necessary facts for the purpose of dispose of this Rule is that the opposite party no. 2 as complainant filed a petition of complaint alleging inter alia that the accused petitioner is his friend and both of them are engaged in business and due to this there was good relationship in between them. The accused petitioner out of this good relationship demanded money from him in connection with his business purpose. As per terms of agreement made by the accused petitioner he paid Tk. 13, 65,500/- on 16.5.95 to the accused petitioner in presence of witnesses nos. 1 and 2 with a promise that he will repay the same within March, 1996. The accused petitioner with a view to misappropriate the money made dilatory tactics in making the repayment. Then there was a salish in his office at Charpara regarding the repayment of money and in this salish the accused petitioner promised to repay the money and accordingly the accused petitioner issued a cheque being no. 0414688 for Tk. 13, 65,500/- on 8.7.96 which was presented to the bank for encashment on 10.7.96. But the cheque was returned un-cashed with the remarks that there was no sufficient fund to honor the cheque. After bouncing of the cheque the accused petitioner in presence of the witnesses promised to repay the money on 13.9.96 but did not repay and refused to repay the money and thereby committed an offence under section 406/420 of the Penal Code. On receipt of the petition of complaint the learned Magistrate by the impugned order dated 14.7.96 issued summons upon the accused petitioner fixing 25.8.96 for return of the same. The accused petitioner obtained anticipatory bail in Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 4217/96 from this Court and after obtaining bail did not appear before the Court of the Magistrate inspite of the order given by the Magistrate for appearance and ultimately the bail was cancelled by the Magistrate by his order dated 16.7.97 who also issued warrant of arrest fixing 16.9.97 for return of the same. It is at this stage the accused petitioner moved this Court and obtained the rule on 21.7.97. 

 6. We have heard the learned advocate for the opposite party no. 2 complainant and the application including the petition of complaint and the order dated 14.7.96 passed by the learned Magistrate taking cognizance of the case under sections 406/420 of the Penal Code and also the order dated 16.7.97 passed by the Magistrate by which the bail of the accused petitioner was cancelled as the accused petitioner has misused the privilege of bail. In the petition of complaint the opposite party no. 2 alleges that he gave an amount of Tk. 13, 65,500/- to the accused petitioner who was in need for running his business and who promised to repay the same within 6th March, 1996 but inspite of such promise the accused petitioner did not repay the same for which there was a salish and in that salish the accused petitioner undertake to repay the money and accordingly he issued the cheque being No. 0414688 dated 8.6.96. In the petition of complaint it is also alleged that the cheque was bounced when presented to the bank and the accused petitioner refused to repay the money on approach. It appears that there was a salish in which the accused petitioner undertake to repay the same and accordingly issued a cheque for Tk. 13, 65,500/- on 8.6.96 but the same was bounced with the remarks that there was no sufficient money to honor the cheque. The accused petitioner as it appears issued cheque knowing full well that he had no money in the account for which it was returned unwashed and this bouncing of cheque itself amounts to cheating as the accused petitioner issued the cheque with intent to decive which prima facie attracts the provision of section 420 of the Penal Code if not section 406 of the said Code and as such the contention of the accused petitioner that there was any business transaction in between the parties and the offence if any is civil liability falls through. 

 7. It appears that rule was issued on 21.07.97 calling upon the opposite parties to show cause as to why the proceeding of C.R. Case No. 237(1)96 should not be quashed. At the time of issuance of the rule the accused petitioner as it appears from the order dated 16.7.97 was not on bail as the bail granted earlier was cancelled on that date with the direction to issue warrant of arrest against the accused petitioner. From this order dated 16.9.97 when the rule was issued. The accused petitioner obtained the rule by suppressing the fact and without surrendering before the court and as such he is a fugitive from justice for which he cannot get any relief in this application. 

 8. In view of the facts and circumstances of the case, we find no ground to quash the proceeding of C.R. Case No. 237(1)96 now pending in the Court of Magistrate First Class, Area 3, Mymensing for which the rule should be discharged. 

 In the result, the rule is discharged. The order dated 21.7.97 staying further proceeding of Court case No. 237(1)97 now pending in the Court of Magistrate. First Class, Area 3, Mymensingh is hereby recalled.
